results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 59 outlined draft units match the controlling idea of their aligned spec paragraph, in spec order; the five callouts are unmatched front matter (KEY POINTS carries the thesis statement as the spec places it).

Five units marked two_ideas (KEY POINTS callout; Concepts ¶4; Concepts ¶8; In Practice ¶1; In Practice ¶3): in each case both ideas are part of the aligned controlling idea (thesis statement; p12; p15a; p32; p34).
Every unit supports S1, S2, S3, S4 or S6 through its section's declared role; the vertical table, public evidence and the part-closing recap are spec'd roles.

Each table is introduced or followed by the sentence that states what it shows (regulation, entity, before/after, ratings, three trade-off tables, vertical, group options); quotations (DSA Art. 30, RFC 9700, UCPD 7(6), CarGurus) are tied to the model; figures carry explanatory captions. Gaps readers found in the integration and vertical tables are recorded under flow_is_followable.

Every declared transition_in is expressed at its boundary, including the 'both' placement into the group section ('which is the subject of the next section' / 'A multi-brand group has three realistic options').

Post level: both readers describe problem → vocabulary → model → alternatives/verticals → tests → group question → judgements, matching problem_solution with prerequisite_order and assertion_evidence_reasoning; no section's position is unclear to either reader; both find the Poland → group handoff smooth. Material lost-thread points are listed as separate failures.

results.quote: Industry practice and published reference models add three more levels:
results.finding: Storefront/profile is a display identity, not a hierarchy level, so calling all three 'levels' makes the reader stop and re-read the list.

results.quote: Only the last two can withdraw one vendor's access to one dealer alone; shared seller credentials are the first to retire.
results.finding: The conclusion is not visible in the table: no column says which options revoke per dealer, and the mTLS row lists 'coarse scopes' as a weakness; readers re-read the table and one is still unsure why a per-vendor API key cannot do the same.

results.quote: The three choices hold in every vertical; their weight shifts.
results.finding: The lead sentence promises the three choices per vertical, but the table is organised by other dimensions and adds a Jobs column that the prose never mentions and no Veldmark brand covers; the link between sentence and table is loose and the Jobs column feels out of place.

results.draft_locus: In Practice: Documented Patterns and Three Veldmark Accounts ¶2
results.quote: When Veldmark ID rolls out in 2028, the same identity gives her a separate Motorvane profile if she ever sells a car, but no Motorvane seller account until she creates one.
results.finding: 'Profile' was defined in Concepts as the storefront (public identity shown to buyers); here it means a per-brand identity profile, so read with the definition the sentence contradicts itself (a public profile without a seller account). The same ambiguity recurs in the group section ('Veldmark ID links profiles across brands').

results.draft_locus: In Practice: Documented Patterns and Three Veldmark Accounts ¶6
results.quote: one of the eight problems Veldmark starts 2027 with
results.finding: Dangling reference to a list outside the chapter, with no link; both readers wondered whether they had missed something.

results.draft_locus: From the Listing to Its Supply ¶2
results.quote: With the seller account modeled, every reference the listing holds has an owner, a version and a contract
results.finding: The chapter never discussed a version of the seller account model, so 'a version' connects to nothing in this chapter until the next sentence names the Part II test; the following paragraph's 'Veldmark Place' is likewise unglossed. A clause linking the account model's version to its event contract (Decision 1) would close it.

results.draft_locus: Architecture: The Seller Account Model ¶3 (before/after table)
results.quote: | Seller accounts on Hearthly | 1 parent advertiser and 13 child advertisers | Six seller accounts, one per legal entity |
results.finding: The Before column says 'One advertiser record for the network', '1 parent advertiser and 13 child advertisers' and '14 advertisers (the parent and 13 children)' in successive rows; the reader had to reconcile the counts to see the parent advertiser doubled as a branch. Single reader.

results.draft_locus: In Practice: Documented Patterns and Three Veldmark Accounts ¶4
results.quote: verified against the commercial register when it signed its contract in 2019, which until Motorvane's June 2027 re-check pilot was the only check Motorvane ran on dealers
results.finding: Ambiguous 'which' needed two readings; 'business claims' in the next sentence is unexplained. Single reader.

results.quote: That seller account is the last subdomain the listing points to
results.finding: 'That seller account' points back to the passing phrase 'in its account' rather than to the listed subdomains, and the sentence then switches to a second idea; reader re-read. Single reader.

results.quote: A user has **memberships**: a relation to an organization
results.finding: Concepts builds memberships around 'organization', the model's table renames it 'Legal entity' and has no membership row, and listings are owned by the seller account and assigned to a branch; the reader could not tell whether a membership attaches to the organization, seller account or branch. Single reader.

results.draft_locus: In Practice: Documented Patterns and Three Veldmark Accounts ¶1
results.quote: Dealers keep their data portable across marketplaces, and the integration-principal model is how a marketplace accepts that.
results.finding: The step from a merger clearance to the integration-principal model is a leap; reader B re-read the bullet. Reader A noted the loose tie but called it not a real block, so not corroborated.

results.quote: In March 2027, Veldmark committed that **no Keybridge agency data is used by Hearthly for ranking or sales targeting**
results.finding: The commitment arrives without its reason (Keybridge holds agencies' data from rival portals, a competition matter), which only the section's last paragraph hints at. Single reader.

results.draft_locus: From the Listing to Its Supply ¶1
results.quote: One advertiser record could not, because it answered four questions at once.
results.finding: Figure 1 gives the advertiser five roles and the model has eight entities; 'four questions' matches the Key Points but made the reader check the count again. Single reader.

results.draft_locus: Setting the Scene at Veldmark: Fourteen Branches, Three Wrong Answers ¶5
results.quote: With Veldmark ID due for approval in June 2027
results.finding: Veldmark ID is used as a deadline driver before the chapter says what it is; it is glossed only later in Users ('the user is a Veldmark ID identity'). Gloss it at first use.
'Bumps' (paid re-promotion of a listing) is used without explanation here and again in Failure Modes item 6.
Opens on the many meanings of 'seller' and the drifting user table, states the claim and a roadmap; none of the weak patterns.
Synthesizes the letter's four problems, closes Part II and hands off to Part III; no new subtopic, no 'in conclusion', not a grab bag.
Each complaint lands on its entity; so-what: later stages read contracts (Veldmark's five 2027 decisions) instead of copying tables.
Returns to Agence Rhône Habitat's letter and to the Part II test, as the spec's callback requires.

The intro reader predicted every section in the post spec's order (scene, vocabulary, model with lifecycle/routing/ratings, alternatives and verticals, public evidence and the three cases, group sharing, failure modes/CA view/questions) and the evidence kinds.
Reader's predicted sections, order and evidence (EU law, public company documents, fictional Veldmark) match the post spec's roadmap; nothing the chapter covers was unpredictable.

Reader names the single cause (one advertiser entity as login, legal identity, billing party, public profile and listing owner) and places trader, reviews, listings/leads and invoices on the right entities; the feed vendor was not in the probe, and Keybridge as integration principal is not required to answer it.

Reader gives the checkbox's missing evidence/date/wording/history and the regimes depending on it, the four-part record with history, and the reclassification process with signals, case, seller response and recorded outcome.

Reader explains indistinguishability, no per-dealer revocation or throttling, password resets breaking feeds, RFC 9700's password-grant ban, and the replacement: one client (or certificate) with grants per seller account, branch and scope, consented and individually revocable.

Reader shares login and registry legal facts, keeps brand accounts separate, excludes packages/prices/leads/listing counts, links accounts to registry not to each other, restricts the cross-brand query to a privileged report, logs and reviews every use, and keeps the software product as an integration principal.
